## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**System Name:** Main House
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a CRITICAL pump problem that requires immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its rated amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This condition poses a risk of motor damage from overheating without fluid cooling. All other components are in good condition and the dispersal field is dry with no surface breakout.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter is in good condition with light soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Measured Amp Draw | 1.6 A |
| Nameplate Rating | 7.2 A |
| Load Percentage | 22.2% FLA |
| Status | CRITICAL - No Load |

The pump is running but drawing only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This indicates the pump is operating with no hydraulic load. The most likely causes are a dry run condition (no fluid reaching the pump), a broken or missing impeller, or a severed or disconnected discharge line. The high water alarm tested functional and electrical connections are sound, ruling out control circuit failure.

The pump motor is at risk of overheating without fluid to provide cooling during operation.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no ponding, breakout, or wet spots observed during the field walk.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE PRIORITY:**
- **Immediate professional attention required.** The effluent pump is drawing 22.2% of rated amperage with no hydraulic load. Do not continue operating the system in this condition. A qualified pump technician must inspect the pump discharge line for disconnection or blockage, check the pump impeller for damage or absence, and verify that fluid is reaching the pump intake. Motor damage from dry-run operation can occur rapidly.

**SECONDARY:**
- Once the pump load problem is resolved and normal operation is restored, recommend measuring dissolved oxygen in the aerobic treatment unit at the next maintenance visit to establish a treatment baseline and confirm biological activity.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure Risk
Your pump is running but not pumping. This is a serious condition. A pump motor without fluid cooling will overheat and fail within hours to days of continuous operation. Do not ignore this problem or defer it. Contact a septic service technician immediately to diagnose and repair the discharge line, impeller, or other cause of the no-load condition.

### Tank Solids
Your tank solids are at 22.9 percent of volume, which is within the normal range. Continue to keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and other items that do not break down naturally. These materials slow the biological process and accelerate solids accumulation.
